examples.label: Example 1
examples.code:
<tp-tikz scale="1.8" label="Linear, sine and exponential functions"><script type="tp/tikz">\begin{tikzpicture}[domain=0:4]
  \draw[very thin,color=gray] (-0.1,-1.1) grid (3.9,3.9);

  \draw[->] (-0.2,0) -- (4.2,0) node[right] {$x$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1.2) -- (0,4.2) node[above] {$f(x)$};

  \draw[color=red]    plot (\x,\x)             node[right] {$f(x) =x$};
  % \x r means to convert '\x' from degrees to _r_adians:
  \draw[color=blue]   plot (\x,{sin(\x r)})    node[right] {$f(x) = \sin x$};
  \draw[color=orange] plot (\x,{0.05*exp(\x)}) node[right] {$f(x) = \frac{1}{20} \mathrm e^x$};
\end{tikzpicture}</script></tp-tikz>

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible title for the drawing frame.

attributes.name: libraries
attributes.description: Comma-separated TikZ libraries to load before the drawing.

attributes.name: scale
attributes.description: Positive display scale for the complete drawing, constrained to the available width.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: URL of a TikZ source file; takes precedence over value and inline source.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: TikZ source; takes precedence over inline source when present.

userHelp.introduction: The custom `<tp-tikz>` element renders TikZ drawings.
userHelp.interactions:
#### Mouse interactions

| Control or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| None | No component-specific mouse interaction; the drawing is static. |

#### Keyboard interactions

| Key or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Open help for the component under the pointer, or the focused component. <kbd>Shift</kbd> may be needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Choose a component in the hierarchy and open its help. |
